descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Numbers — Mental Math and Algorithms to 1000, Multiplication and Division to 10×10, Fractions as Repeated Addition, and Ratios 1:2 / 1:5 / 1:10 (B2.1–B2.9)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.B2.1: use the properties of operations, and the relationships between multiplication and division, to solve problems and check calculations
curriculum_expectations.B2.2: recall and demonstrate multiplication facts of 2, 5, and 10, and related division facts
curriculum_expectations.B2.3: use mental math strategies, including estimation, to add and subtract whole numbers that add up to no more than 1000, and explain the strategies used
curriculum_expectations.B2.4: demonstrate an understanding of algorithms for adding and subtracting whole numbers by making connections to and describing the way other tools and strategies are used to add and subtract
curriculum_expectations.B2.5: represent and solve problems involving the addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 1000, using various tools and algorithms
curriculum_expectations.B2.6: represent multiplication of numbers up to 10 × 10 and division up to 100 ÷ 10, using a variety of tools and drawings, including arrays
curriculum_expectations.B2.7: represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division, including problems that involve groups of one half, one fourth, and one third, using tools and drawings
curriculum_expectations.B2.8: represent the connection between the numerator of a fraction and the repeated addition of the unit fraction with the same denominator using tools, drawings, and standard fractional notation
curriculum_expectations.B2.9: use the ratios of 1 to 2, 1 to 5, and 1 to 10 to scale up numbers and to solve problems

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on operations framed around 'The Times Table Toolkit' — Tony the Toolkit Master and Maya the Multiplication Maven. Day 1 'Mental Math and Algorithms to 1000' covers B2.3, B2.4, B2.5 — chunking, the standard algorithm, and story-problem modelling. Day 2 'The 2s, 5s, 10s Toolkit' anchors the multiplication facts of 2, 5, 10 with arrays and the related division facts (B2.2, B2.1). Day 3 'Multiplication to 10×10' extends to all multiplication facts and division to 100÷10 using arrays and skip-counting (B2.6). Day 4 'Numerator as Repeated Addition' connects fractions to multiplication: 3/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4, and groups of fractional sizes (B2.8, B2.7). Day 5 'Ratios — Scale It Up' closes with ratios 1:2, 1:5, 1:10 in real-world contexts (B2.9). The unit progresses concrete (arrays, fraction strips, ratio tables) → representational (multiplication tables, tape diagrams) → abstract (algorithms, ratio notation).
unit_learning_goal: Children will use mental math and algorithms to add and subtract to 1000, recall multiplication facts of 2, 5, 10 (with related division), represent multiplication to 10×10 and division to 100÷10, see numerators as repeated addition of unit fractions, and use ratios 1:2, 1:5, 1:10 to scale.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can add and subtract numbers to 1000 using mental chunking OR the standard algorithm. Both give the same answer.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can add and subtract numbers to 1000 using mental chunking and the standard algorithm.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tony's mental-chunking warm-up; introduce the standard algorithm with regrouping; story problems to 1000.

lesson_arc.big_idea: The 2s, 5s, and 10s multiplication facts are anchors — and each fact triangle has 4 facts (2 multiplications + 2 divisions).
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can recall multiplication facts of 2, 5, and 10 and write the related division facts.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maya's array warm-up; fact-family triangle work; rapid-recall stations for ×2, ×5, ×10 and ÷2, ÷5, ÷10.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Every multiplication fact up to 10×10 can be shown as an array. Division up to 100÷10 is the inverse.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can represent any multiplication fact up to 10×10 as an array and find the related division.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Multiplication chart 1-10; array building for 6×7, 8×9, 7×8; division as inverse (49÷7=7).

lesson_arc.big_idea: The numerator of a fraction tells us how many copies of the unit fraction. 3/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4. We can also see groups of 1/2 or 1/4 as multiplication.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can show that 3/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 and 4 × 1/2 = 2 wholes using fraction strips.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tony's fraction-strip stacking; 3/4 = three 1/4s; 4 × 1/2 = 2 wholes; group-of-fraction multiplication.

lesson_arc.big_idea: A ratio compares two amounts. 1:2 means 'for every 1, there are 2'. We can scale up to find new amounts.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use ratios 1:2, 1:5, and 1:10 to scale up amounts and solve real-life problems.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maya's ratio table — '1 cup of flour to 2 cups of milk' scaled up to 5 cups of flour; 1:5 and 1:10 ratios in recipes and money.

recurring_characters.name: Tony the Toolkit Master
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Anchors Lessons 1, 4, 5 — the operations and fractions/ratios work. Loves tools and tools-as-metaphor for math strategies.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A maker-style character with a tool belt holding rulers, calculators, and fraction strips. Wears a striped apron with a × symbol patch. Short hair, smart eyes, friendly smile.

recurring_characters.name: Maya the Multiplication Maven
recurring_characters.role: Tony's partner. Anchors Lessons 2 and 3 — the multiplication facts work. Specialises in array thinking and skip-counting.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A creative-looking character with a sketch pad covered in arrays and fact triangles. Wears a vest with multiplication-table patches, eyeglasses, eager smile.

recurring_characters.name: Pixel the Practice Pal
recurring_characters.role: A small helper character who appears at every station. Carries a flash card with the fact of the moment. Cameo across all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A tiny robot-like character with a screen for a face displaying the current math fact. Bouncy walk, encouraging beeps.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: A step-by-step recipe for solving a problem. The standard algorithm for adding numbers stacks them in columns and adds digit by digit.
To trade — like trading 10 ones for 1 ten when adding. Sometimes called carrying.
Equal groups arranged in rows and columns. 4 rows of 3 dots is an array showing 4 × 3 = 12.
A number being multiplied. In 4 × 3 = 12, the factors are 4 and 3.
The total when you multiply. In 4 × 3 = 12, the product is 12.
A fraction with 1 on the top: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4. The numerator is always 1.
A way to compare two amounts. 1:2 means 'for every 1 of one thing, there are 2 of another'.
To multiply both parts of a ratio by the same number. 1:2 scaled up by 5 is 5:10.

assessment_strategy.diagnostic: Lesson 1 mental math snapshot: each child solves 5 sums and 5 differences in the 100-1000 range. Tally chunking-vs-algorithm strategies and accuracy.
assessment_strategy.formative: Lesson 2 fact-recall tracker for ×2, ×5, ×10. Lesson 3 array tracker for ×6, ×7, ×8, ×9. Lesson 4 fraction-as-addition tracker.
assessment_strategy.summative: Lesson 5 Ratios worksheet — 3 ratio scaling problems (1:2, 1:5, 1:10) plus a real-life context. Captures B2.9 and pulls in B2.7.

pedagogical_notes: B2.2 (facts of 2, 5, 10) are the gateway facts. Skip-counting by 2s, 5s, 10s gives the multiplication directly.
B2.3 + B2.4 + B2.5 are integrated in Lesson 1: mental chunking is the strategy; the standard algorithm is the formal version; story problems contextualise both.
B2.6 (multiplication to 10×10) is the conceptual peak. Children should see multiplication as both equal groups AND arrays.
B2.7 'groups of one half, one fourth, one third' is the fractional multiplication extension. 4 × 1/2 = 2 wholes is the key example.
B2.8 (numerator as repeated addition) is the fraction-as-multiplication insight. 3/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3 × 1/4.
B2.9 (ratios 1:2, 1:5, 1:10) introduces ratio notation and scaling. Children should see ratios as 'for every X there are Y' and scale by multiplication.
canadian_context_notes: Recipe ratios are a real-life Canadian context (1 cup flour to 2 cups milk for pancakes).
Money ratios connect to currency (1 toonie = 2 dollars; 1 quarter = 5 nickels; 1 dime = 10 pennies historically).
Sports stats: ratios in hockey scoring (1:2 wins to losses, etc.)
Multiplication is foundational for all later math, so anchor it strongly here.
